items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: the melody was from Samuel Augustus Ward, and then Katharine Lee Bates.

ctx.x: I think it’s curious, those controversial performances, the “Star Spangled Banner” and these sports teams or whatever, they hire these people and then they’re so surprised and sometimes angry when the person sings like they do. Like you were expecting Marvin Gaye to sing the national anthem like an opera singer or like someone with great respect. And he sings it like he wants to and everybody gets bent out of shape. And it’s just curious that, well why are you hiring these people then, if you don’t want them to…

Yeah. And I mean that was Marvin Gaye who won the coveted Grammy award for “Sexual Healing.” And then the ironic part is that the melody of the “Star Spangled Banner” by John Stafford Smith was an 18th century British sex and drinking song, so actually and ironically Marvin Gaye was actually respecting the tradition of where it came from, which is actually Brit — I mean “America the Beautiful,” actually that was by two composers — the melody was from Samuel Augustus Ward, and then Katharine Lee Bates. And that’s…

I mean he had Aretha Franklin sing “My Country ‘Tis of Thee,” which is actually only like six pitches in range, vocal range, an easy song to sing.
